bottom_line: Tech and AI stocks just had their worst week since 2020, and at the same time markets are betting the Fed (the people who set interest rates) will RAISE rates in December, not cut them. Falling stock prices plus pricier borrowing is the squeeze everyone is talking about.

stories.title: AI stocks had a brutal week
stories.real: Tech stocks got hammered in their worst week since Covid. Nvidia closed out its longest weekly losing streak since 2008, Amazon slid, and Anthropic's record IPO (its first day selling shares to the public) landed right in the middle of it. One headline called it an 8% weekly crash.

stories.title: The Fed looks ready to raise rates
stories.real: Fed meeting notes say higher interest rates are needed in December because inflation worries are growing. Markets are betting over 90% odds of a December hike, and J.P. Morgan changed its call too.
stories.you: A rate hike usually means loans, credit cards and mortgages cost more, while savings accounts can pay a bit more.

stories.title: Trump is fighting the Fed
stories.real: Trump says interest rates are too high and accuses the Fed of acting politically. He wants rates cut to the world's lowest and pointed to India's 7% growth to make his case. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is stuck between the president and inflation.
stories.you: The president wants cheaper borrowing, but the Fed sets rates, and right now it is leaning the other way.

stories.title: Push to cap credit card rates
stories.real: Trump says he will work with Democrats to cap credit card interest rates at 10%. This is a promise for now, not a law.
stories.you: If it ever passed, people who carry a credit card balance would pay less interest. Nothing changes on your card today.

stories.title: Shoppers holding up, but cracks show
stories.real: US consumers are still spending going into the holiday season even with high prices. More people filed for unemployment aid, but the number is still low historically. New inflation numbers come out this week, and some are warning about recession risk.
stories.you: Jobs are mostly holding for now, but prices are still a strain, so this week's inflation report matters for your budget.
